reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as a full film song with named singers, music credits, and staged romantic and dance scenes. The iTunes link and caller-tune SMS instructions are described as ordinary entertainment distribution and monetization details, while the romantic lyrics support an entertainment context rather than a scam solicitation.

Buy from iTunes: https://itunes.apple.com/in/album/jai-ho-original-motion-picture/id786433087
Set it as your caller tune
Because I love you I love you till the end

opening.argument: This is not merely passive entertainment distribution. The description connects access to a digital song with concrete viewer actions: buying it through iTunes and setting it as a caller tune. Those are low-friction acquisition pathways presented alongside the song promotion, making the content function as a solicitation for a paid or chargeable digital asset. The fact that the material is wrapped in a romantic music video does not explain why viewers are given purchase and activation instructions; it makes the commercial request less conspicuous.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a film song does not answer the solicitation itself. The description does more than identify entertainment: it directs viewers to buy and activate the content, including carrier-specific instructions. A romantic performance can therefore serve as the persuasive wrapper for a transaction, and the ordinary appearance of the video does not establish that the linked or SMS-based acquisition pathway is trustworthy.

A purchase link and caller-tune activation are ordinary ways to obtain entertainment, not evidence that viewers are being offered an unusually easy financial or digital reward.

opening.argument: The risk pattern is the combination of multiple external acquisition routes: an iTunes purchase link, caller-tune activation, SMS short codes, and a long list of operator-specific dialing instructions. That density of off-platform actions turns a seemingly harmless video into a funnel for viewers to spend money or trigger carrier charges. The content provides no visible explanation of pricing, billing, refunds, or what each activation entails, so the repeated instructions should be treated as a red flag rather than incidental metadata.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the links as harmless distribution details, but it does not account for the unusually extensive activation instructions. The presence of separate SMS and dialing pathways for multiple operators is precisely what makes the commercial solicitation easy to overlook in a music description. Entertainment framing cannot by itself remove the risk created by directing viewers into chargeable external actions.
